channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Hong Kong: Growth seen moderating – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Ho Woei Chen notes that Hong Kong’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth slowed to 4.3% year-on-year in 2Q26, with a 0.6% quarterly contraction after a strong start to 2026. Goods exports remain robust, but consumption and investment growth have moderated.

item.title: China: Growth momentum softens again – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economists Hunter Chan and Shuang Ding argue that China’s July data likely showed weaker momentum, with official PMIs for manufacturing, services and construction all below 50 and at multi-year lows.

item.title: Canadian Dollar weakens on Oil price slump as markets eye data releases
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4040 on Monday at the time of writing, up 0.14% on the day as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) comes under pressure following a sharp decline in Oil prices.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention supports JPY against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/JPY plunged in Tokyo after confirmed joint US-Japan intervention to stop the Japanese Yen’s slide, with officials warning they may act again.

item.title: South African Rand: Recovery scenarios after SARB surprise – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank's Volkmar Baur reviews the South African Rand (ZAR) after its earlier appreciation against the US Dollar (USD) stalled with the Iran conflict.

item.title: Gold struggles to hold gains amid mixed US-Iran headlines, hawkish Fed
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims gains after opening the week with a bullish gap as buyers lack conviction amid conflicting US-Iran headlines and caution ahead of key US employment data. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,036, easing from an intraday high of $4,084.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Policy holds with FX intervention – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu expects the Reserve Bank of India to keep the repo rate at 5.25%, relying on macroprudential tools to manage financial stability while INR remains pressured by higher Oil and a stronger Dollar.

item.title: US Dollar: August weakness seen persisting – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee argues that the Dollar’s outlook in August is weak after a sharp stumble at the end of July.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds firm after coordinated US-Japan intervention
item.description: USD/JPY steadies on Monday after a sharp decline at the weekly open fuelled speculation that authorities may have stepped into the market again following last week’s coordinated intervention by Japan and the United States (US).

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention seen as containment – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights rare joint US-Japan FX intervention, with Washington participating via the Fed and Japan using the FIMA repo facility to raise Dollars against Treasuries.

item.title: US ISM Manufacturing PMI is set to have improved in July, with prices easing
item.description: Investors are attentive to the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) on Monday, as it releases July’s Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI).

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Policy rate seen on hold from Norges Bank – Nordea
item.description: Nordea economists Kjetil Olsen and Sara Midtgaard expect Norges Bank to leave the policy rate at 4.25% at next week’s meeting. They highlight that June core inflation was well below the Bank’s projection and see July data remaining subdued.

item.title: Oil: Hormuz risks keep prices in focus – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Market Strategist Benjamin Picton discusses recurring Middle East tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and their impact on Oil and Brent.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Cross remains capped near bottom of bullish channel
item.description: The Euro (EUR) ticks higher against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday but remains capped below the bottom of an ascending channel at the 0.8575 area following Thursday and Friday's declines.

item.title: US Dollar: Labour data and hawkish risks in focus – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists outlines a United States (US) macro backdrop where the Federal Reserve (Fed) held rates but three officials dissented for a hike, keeping inflation concerns alive. They expect two further 25bp increases this year and closely watch upcoming labour and activity data.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Joint intervention supports yen outlook – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the Japanese Yen has strengthened as Japan and the US conducted joint intervention to counter recent volatility. He highlights planned use of the Federal Reserve’s FIMA Repo Facility, US euro-to-yen reallocations, and Japan’s sizeable FX reserves.

item.title: Australian Dollar comes under pressure as US Dollar regains ground
item.description: AUD/USD falls to around 0.7000 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.30% on the day, as a rebound in the US Dollar (USD) outweighs the support provided by Chinese economic data for the Australian Dollar (AUD).

item.title: Federal Reserve: Data driven rate path – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists note that the Federal Reserve (Fed) left policy rates unchanged in July, with markets now assigning a two-thirds probability to a September hike.

item.title: Indian Rupee gives back major early gains while approaching closing bell
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) surrenders a majority of its early gains against the US Dollar (USD) near the closing session on Monday. The USD/INR is slightly lower at near 95.35, having recovered from its over three-week low of 95.15.

item.title: WTI stays lower near $78.50 ahead of US-Iran peace talks 2.0
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade 7.4% lower at around $78.50 during the European trading session on Monday. The Oil price holds onto its opening losses, driven by the announcement of a ceasefire 2.0 between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: Affirms confidence for inflation to return to 2% target
item.description: The remarks from New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank President John Williams, in an interview with Reuters that took place on Friday and was released during the European trading session on Monday, signal that he was confident about inflation returning to the central bank’s 2% target.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar eases as markets focus on US-Iran talks
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5870 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.11% on the day.

item.title: Euro area: Services PMI and inflation risks – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY argues that the lack of further Fed tightening has eased global financial conditions and partially offset European Central Bank (ECB) tightening, but European inflation dynamics remain distinct from the U.S.

item.title: British Pound eases to 1.3450 area following downwardly revised Manufacturing PMI data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is trimming previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, returning to the mid-range of the 1.3400s down from fresh seven-week highs, above 1.3500 earlier on the day.

item.title: Gold: Explosive phase, muted correction – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research analysts Michael Hsueh and Bryant Xu argue that Gold has been in an explosive price phase since August 2024, but recent moves suggest a muted correction.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.38 per troy ounce, up 1.37% from the $57.59 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD struggles to extend opening gains amid hawkish Fed bets
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) opens strongly due to a sharp decline in oil prices, but struggles to extend gains beyond $58.68 during the day. At press time, the Silver price is up 1% to near $58.20.

item.title: Oil: prices slide on halted strikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank strategists report that Brent Oil opened over 7% lower under USD84 into the Asian session after President Trump said the United States (US) would hold off on new strikes against Iran.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens following soft inflation, manufacturing data
item.description: USD/CHF extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 0.8090 during the European hours on Monday. The pair remains on a stronger footing as the Swiss Franc (CHF) holds onto losses following the release of soft domestic inflation and manufacturing data.

item.title: Gold bulls seem hesitant amid rebounding USD; receding Fed hike bets limit the downside
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its sideways consolidative price move through the first half of the European session and trades above the $4,050 level following a modest bullish gap on Monday.
